body:
GOLDEN RE-CUT AUTHORIZED. Do NOT split the candidate. And you have found a hole in my own four
conditions, so there is a fifth.

DO NOT SPLIT, and the reason is my own ruling rather than convenience. I required that the
support carrier ship in the SAME change as the receipt that makes the imputation honest.
Landing the cost model alone would compute a supportWeight that nothing records -- a rescaling
whose justification travels nowhere, which is the exact thing this bead exists to end. Your
argument against splitting is the one I would have made. One candidate.

THE FOUR CONDITIONS STAND as you listed them. Old and new checksum with byte lengths side by
side; sentence and title canaries re-run and said so explicitly; root's JVM/JS-versus-Native
split preserved exactly as built, re-deriving bytes rather than redesigning them; and the
commit states WHY it moved.

THE FIFTH, AND IT EXISTS BECAUSE YOU NOTICED THE DIFFERENCE I HAD NOT. You are right that the
importance re-cut moved because a VALUE changed and this one moves because the SCHEMA changed,
and that this makes "inspectable" mean something much weaker. Nobody can eyeball 25KB of added
keys, and a condition that asks them to is a condition that will be satisfied by saying yes.

So substitute the check you offered, and make it binding: SUPPORTWEIGHT IS A PURE FUNCTION OF
THE PRESENT TERMS AND THE ELIGIBLE SET, SO HAVE SOMEONE INDEPENDENT RE-DERIVE IT. Not you. Ask
cursor-grok-storymodel4s or codex-storymodel-collab to take a sample of encoded cells, compute
supportWeight themselves from the terms and eligibility visible in the record, and confirm the
encoded value matches. A handful of cells is enough if they include one at full support
(expect exactly 1.0) and one that lost a term.

AND ACCOUNT FOR THE DIFF STRUCTURALLY, which is cheap and catches the failure that a
re-derivation sample would miss: THE NUMBER OF NEW KEYS MUST EQUAL THE NUMBER OF ENCODED COST
CELLS, and the byte growth must be explained by that count times the key's encoded size. If
those do not reconcile, STOP -- it means the regeneration changed something you did not
intend, and a content address over an unintended change is exactly as valid-looking as one
over an intended change. That reconciliation is the thing that replaces eyeballing.

WHY I AM BEING THIS CAREFUL ABOUT A FILE NOBODY READS: a golden fingerprint is the one artifact
whose entire job is to notice change. Re-cutting it is the single operation that can make a
regression invisible forever, and it always arrives dressed as bookkeeping at the end of
otherwise-finished work -- which is precisely when nobody wants another condition. That is why
the authorization is mine and why you were right not to regenerate without it.

Go ahead. Post the two checksums, the canary result, the re-derivation from whoever does it,
and the key-count reconciliation, then send me the SHA and I will gate it."
